summary: Hail, convective wind and wildfire have curves built from borrowed and our judgment evidence (hail: 3 parts, convective wind: one curve for the whole building and wildfire: one curve for the whole building); flood and hurricane wind have curves built from published evidence (one curve for the whole building each). All of them are proposals, not in the runtime index yet. 1 part of the building has no curve under any hazard: contents and inventory.
summary_v0: Hail, flood, hurricane wind, convective wind and wildfire are proposals not yet in the runtime index; nobody has yet searched for field reports.

hazards.label: Heat
hazards.effect_note: The twin's heat leads (ageing, derating, chiller capacity) work through performance, not physical damage; pointer to the outage-as-performance work, no curve (discussion 04 §6).

hazards.label: Icing
hazards.effect_note: Two leads in the twin: snow load on the venting panels (physical, L) and cold limiting the charge rate until heated (performance, L). No hazard cell; the C-172 snow-and-ice reasoning applies (discussion 04 §6).

hazards.label: Lightning
hazards.effect_note: No hazard cell exists; the twin carries Medium surge leads on the electronics (discussion 04 §6).

split.sentence: These cells split the building differently: the cells name different numbers of parts: convective wind 4, flood 5, hail 7, hurricane wind 5 and wildfire 4; hail splits each building into the roof and the walls and windows, each a share of the building's value; the other hazards price the building as one; retail has a curve under flood and hurricane wind only; convective wind, hail and wildfire do not name it. Buildings carry no dollar value here: every curve is a share of the building's structure replacement cost, which the consumer supplies.
